newsitem.title: INDIA: At least 119 people killed so far in Delhi fever.
newsitem.headline: At least 119 people killed so far in Delhi fever.

text.p: At least 119 people have been been killed so far in an outbreak of dengue fever that has affected hundreds in the Indian capital, medical and government officials said on Saturday.
"The total number of deaths reported so far has been 119," Dr Sanju Kohli, senior medical officer at the Dengue control room, told Reuters.

Some 2,194 people have been infected in the Indian capital by the dengue fever since the first death was reported on August 29, officials said. There have been no reports of the disease outside the capital so far.
Dengue, also called breakbone fever, is normally accompanied by high fever, headaches and pain in muscles and joints. It runs its course in six to seven days.
Dengue is usually carried by the Aedes aegypti mosquito, which breeds in stagnant water, especially in air coolers and other water-filled objects in residences in New Delhi.
"The government is taking steps to clear breeding grounds of mosquitos in stagnant water, filth and garbage," Kohli said.
But he said city residents also had to ensure that their surrounding environment remained clean.
